title: Letter from Paul Reiner, attorney for Hedy Lamarr (Mrs. Hedwig Loder), to the U.S. Reparations, Deliveries and Restitution Division, Austria, 7 December 1945 (page 1)
creator: Paul Reiner, attorney, New York
institution: National Archives and Records Administration, Records of U.S. Occupation Headquarters, World War II (file M-92)
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives and Records Administration, National Archives Identifier 74395327
alt_text: Typed 1945 letter asking U.S. officials in Austria to protect Lamarr's inherited oil-field share.
long_description: Typewritten letter on Paul Reiner letterhead, 19 Rector Street, New York, dated December 7th 1945, with receipt stamps of 27 and 28 December 1945 and handwritten notes 'British' and 'Russian zone'. It states he writes 'as the attorney for Miss Hedy Lamarr of 2702 Benedict Canyon, Beverly Hills, California who by marriage became Mrs. Hedwig Loder and who is a British subject', and describes her father Emil Kiesler's 30% share in oil-drilling companies at Zistersdorf, inherited by her as his only child on his death in 1935.
gloss: Eight years after she left: Vienna, her father's legacy, and her nationality, in one letter.

title: Letter from Paul Reiner, attorney for Hedy Lamarr, 7 December 1945 (page 2)
creator: Paul Reiner, attorney, New York
institution: National Archives and Records Administration (file M-92)
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives and Records Administration, National Archives Identifier 74395327
alt_text: Second page of the 1945 letter, on the Red Army seizing the Zistersdorf oil field.
long_description: Typewritten page II, signed by Paul Reiner. Says that since 7 December 1941 she had been unable to correspond with the oil fields, cites a New York Times report that the Red Army had taken possession of the Zistersdorf field, and asks for protection because, 'as an American resident, for the time being, she is unable to take any other steps directly in Austria.'
gloss: The war cut her off from home; the peace handed her inheritance to the Soviets.
